papers.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a powerful approach for improving language-model reasoning, but its supervision is inherently sparse: a sequence-level verifier reward is propagated only through sampled trajectories and provides no direct signal for alternative actions. On-policy distillation (OPD) offers a complementary form of supervision by providing dense teacher feedback over the full next-token distribution, but this signal is not grounded in verified task outcomes. Simply co-optimizing the two objectives does not couple these signals: verifier feedback remains sparse and does not inform the dense teacher supervision. We introduce Verifiable On-Policy Distillation (VOPD), which transfers sparse verifier feedback into dense, verifier-grounded supervision. Our key observation is that the implicit-reward view of OPD places teacher supervision and verifier feedback in a common reward space while retaining a reward signal available for every next-token action. Under this view, VOPD projects verifier preference onto the teacher's implicit-reward direction and Rao--Blackwellizes the resulting signal over the full vocabulary, propagating verifier-grounded supervision to actions that were never sampled. The resulting objective can also be interpreted as adaptively extrapolating the distillation target according to teacher--verifier agreement. Across two teacher--student configurations and eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VOPD consistently improves both final performance and learning efficiency over vanilla OPD and other on-policy distillation baselines. Our code is available at https://github.com/juntongshi48/VOPD.

summary.en: VOPD projects sparse verifier preferences onto the teacher's implicit-reward direction and Rao-Blackwellizes them over the vocabulary for dense verifier-grounded supervision, improving final performance and learning efficiency over vanilla OPD and other on-policy distillation baselines on eight math reasoning benchmarks.
summary.zh: VOPD 将稀疏的验证器奖励投影到教师的隐式奖励方向上，并在整个词表上做 Rao-Blackwell 化，得到稠密的、基于验证器的监督信号，在八项数学推理基准上相比 vanilla OPD 与其他 on-policy distillation 基线同时提升最终性能与学习效率。

papers.title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly work as teams of agents, and a team is expected to solve problems beyond the reach of any single member. Most evaluations credit a team for outperforming a single agent, without accounting for the additional computation: a team may consume many times the tokens of one agent, and a plain vote over independent answers already explains most of the reported gain. Two questions therefore remain open: When does interaction itself make a group smarter, and can a group improve its next generation by learning from its own work? We answer both with the equal-budget ladder, which grades a group against independent agents at three levels: outperforming a single agent, a compute-matched majority vote, and compute-matched pass@n. On this ladder we define Recursive Collective Intelligence (RCI) as a group whose own output, without a teacher or external labels, makes its next generation smarter at equal cost. Three findings follow. First, interaction improves collective intelligence when it moves information across agents: forwarding split facts lifts groups above pass@n at three model scales, by about a third at 27B. Second, organization emerges spontaneously: identical 27B agents form hubs and improve accuracy by 18 percentage points; encoding their organization in a prompt enables them to reach level 3 at less than half the token budget in a descriptive comparison. Third, groups recursively improve themselves: Two label-free generations progressively climb the ladder, the second 9B generation surpassing both pass@$n$ and a control trained on base-model turns; on PlanBench, HiddenBench and Hanabi, each generation outperforms its predecessor on unseen problems for four to six generations. A group therefore outperforms its members when it forwards useful information more efficiently than it spends tokens on coordination, and learns to do so from its own work.

summary.en: The equal-budget ladder grades multi-agent LLM teams against a single agent, compute-matched majority vote, and pass@n; recursively self-trained groups, which forward split facts, beat pass@n by ~1/3 at 27B, gain 18 points from emergent hubs, and improve for 4-6 generations.
summary.zh: 等算力阶梯（equal-budget ladder），在单智能体、算力对齐多数投票与算力对齐 pass@n 三级上衡量多智能体团队，并定义 Recursive Collective Intelligence（RCI）：无教师、无外部标签，团队用自身输出让下一代同等成本更聪明；转发拆分事实可在 27B 上超 pass@n 约三分之一，同质 27B 智能体自发形成枢纽使准确率提升 18 个百分点，两代无标签训练在 PlanBench、HiddenBench、Hanabi 上连续 4–6 代优于前代。

papers.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
papers.abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are post-trained and deployed as agents inside a "harness", but standard harness designs accumulate context that the neural network is forced to generalize to, making training for long-horizon tasks expensive and time-consuming. We study an alternative emerging path: training inherently neurosymbolic LM harnesses, which externalize and manage context programmatically to compose existing LM capabilities. We hypothesize that training around these harnesses can offer a better return on compute by enabling compositional generalization, as they can learn to decompose complex problems so that every observation their neural LM receives is locally in-distribution, even when the full task is novel. We find that harnesses like the Recursive Language Model (RLM) learn such decompositions readily under reinforcement learning post-training: (1) we demonstrate that training only on short tasks can generalize to tasks 2-64$\times$ longer while the base neural LM improves less, and (2) training on one domain transfers to novel domains that share latent structure. On messier, complex tasks, we find that we can target individual LLM calls within a harness by generating and training on easier, synthetically generated surrogate environments with fake tool / sub-calls, a technique we call surrogate harness training. From this finding, we train RLM-27B on synthetic data, and show it improves Qwen3.8-27B in the same RLM harness on a hard suite of long-context tasks like CTC-Bench and ExpertLongBench by 26.9% on average while using $\sim$2$\times$ fewer tokens at inference time. Finally, we show that harnesses can compose over these newly learned decompositions using recursive sub-harness calls.

summary.en: Training neurosymbolic LM harnesses like RLM with RL on short tasks generalizes to 2-64x longer ones; RLM-27B, trained on synthetic data, beats Qwen3.8-27B by 26.9% on CTC-Bench and ExpertLongBench with ~2x fewer inference tokens.
summary.zh: 研究以神经符号式 harness 管理上下文的组合泛化能力：仅用短任务强化学习训练 RLM，即可泛化到长 2-64 倍的任务；用合成数据训练 RLM-27B，在 CTC-Bench 和 ExpertLongBench 上平均提升 Qwen3.8-27B 26.9%，推理 token 约减半。

papers.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
papers.abstract: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid ($>250\times$ dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension ($d \to d+K$) with $\sqrt{d/(d+K)}$ norm compensation, Base-1000 canonical BPE emission, and differential $(+254,-256)$ tied unembeddings. An automated 5-stage compiler synthesizes 4-8 digit signed $\{+,-,\times\}$ circuits in constant $\mathsf{TC}^0$ depth alongside 3-literal Boolean (100%, $N=1{,}728$; plus 42-layer Gemma 4 E4B audits) and 5-bit Majority/Parity (100%) circuits. On 6-digit arithmetic ($N=1{,}200$, BF16), IBM Granite 4.2 3B (1.07M-1.33M active non-zeros, $\le 0.036\%$) and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B (2.25M-2.39M non-zeros, $\le 0.057\%$) reach 99.17% and 100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy (100% with an FP32 sidecar) and 98%-100% mid-sentence resumption, outperforming 12.8K-sample LoRA (42.2% / 61.7%, 0% inline continuation). A factorized block-sparse sidecar holds A100 memory at 7.89 / 10.65 GiB (4.60 / 8.14 GiB under INT8/INT4 + FP32 sidecar) while passing all 14/14 pre-registered $>2$K-token Tango splits ($N=4{,}392$; 0/11,134 OOD triggers).

summary.en: Closed-form zero-gradient circuit-grafting compiles exact multi-digit arithmetic and Boolean/majority circuits into pretrained LM weights without training data or runtime hooks; Granite 4.2 3B and Qwen 3.5 4B reach 99.17%/100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy versus 42.2%/61.7% for 12.8K-sample LoRA.
summary.zh: 闭式零梯度电路嫁接原语将精确多位数算术与布尔/多数/奇偶电路直接编译进预训练权重，无需训练样本或运行时钩子；IBM Granite 4.2 3B 与 Qwen 3.5 4B 在 6 位数算术上达 99.17%/100.00% ALU 前缀准确率，远超 12.8K 样本 LoRA 的 42.2%/61.7%。

papers.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT

summary.en: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer reuses keys and values as memory across depths and loops; U-MoLT beats OLMo3 with 1.7x CE token efficiency at 700M and +2.1 points on 10-task accuracy at 3B MoE.
summary.zh: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer 用 Mixture-of-Loops Attention 把 KV 当作跨深度和循环复用记忆，其 U-MoLT 变体在 400B token 预训练中于 700M 模型上比 OLMo3 达到 1.7 倍的验证交叉熵 token 效率，3B MoE 困惑度降低 0.75、10 项任务准确率提升 2.1 个百分点。

papers.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
papers.abstract: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention. To enable efficient inference, we further develop an execution scheme tailored to this architecture, combining CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and execution-flow simplification while preserving the canonical history update. Evaluations on retargeted HiPHI demonstrate accurate terminal control over rollouts of up to 39.52 s, while short-horizon comparisons on BONES Seed and retargeted HumanML3D show that the model also retains strong spatial control and text-motion matching. On an RTX 4090, the optimized execution reduces median complete-window latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms, achieving a median paired speedup of 6.138$\times$ while preserving identical outputs and committed states in the tested rollouts. Moreover, we conduct extensive real-world evaluation on the Unitree G1, demonstrating sequential text-guided action composition, expressive motion, and interactive locomotion through keyboard and mouse control.

summary.en: Motion Mamba 2.0 combines Mamba recurrent states with persistent content memory for autoregressive root-body diffusion, enabling terminal control over 39.52 s rollouts; CUDA Graph optimizations cut latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms (6.138x median speedup), validated on Unitree G1.
summary.zh: Motion Mamba 2.0 用 Mamba 循环状态加持久内容记忆 PCM 做根-身体扩散式自回归动作生成，支持最长 39.52 s 的长程末端控制；配合 CUDA Graph 等优化，RTX 4090 上完整窗口延迟从 1685.35 ms 降到 276.14 ms，中位加速 6.138 倍，并在 Unitree G1 上验证了文本引导动作组合与交互式行走。

papers.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
papers.abstract: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/

summary.en: Depth Pro 2 trains one scalable network on images and video to predict native-resolution depth that is metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent, outperforming prior work and redefining the Pareto frontier.
summary.zh: Depth Pro 2 用单一可扩展网络统一处理图像与视频，以原生分辨率预测稠密深度，同时兼顾度量精度、边界锐利度与时序一致性，在四项指标上超越先前方法并重划 Pareto 前沿。

papers.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.

summary.en: Mind2Act World is a 30-task, 180-configuration diagnostic manipulation benchmark with Mind, Act, and Mind2Act views; the best agent scores 52.7% and 39.0% but only 12.0% on Mind2Act.
summary.zh: Mind2Act World 构建 30 个仿真操作任务、180 种配置的诊断基准，分 Mind、Act、Mind2Act 三视角评测多模态智能体、VLA 与 WAM；最强智能体在 Mind 与 Act 上分别成功 52.7% 和 39.0%，Mind2Act 仅 12.0%。

papers.title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act
papers.abstract: Robot policies act in real time but fail without knowing why, whereas a reasoning agent that watches the robot can often tell what went wrong. Existing systems either hand the agent control, which takes minutes per episode, or let it send instructions. Yet a policy follows a new instruction only from a fresh start, since a half-finished task leaves it in states outside its training data. Nor can an instruction fix how the robot moves. If a drift keeps pulling the hand to the left, "push right, slightly" is not a task the policy has learned. We propose RoboThink, in which the agent thinks and the policy learns to act on the agent's guidance. An instruction channel tells the policy what to do. When the user says "the milk, not the butter" after the robot has started, the agent rewrites the instruction and the robot undoes its own motion, with no training. A feedback channel tells it how to move. It is taught from the agent alone with agent-labelled DAgger, role tokens and counterfactual feedback, and is read only by the policy's action module. On LIBERO, RoboThink with Claude Opus 5.5 raises success from 0.09 to 0.87 under an unknown constant drift and from 0.42 to 0.84 under a random one. It also completes misheard and changed requests in 0.91 to 1.00 of the episodes. Acting alone, GPT-6 Astra needs 2.1 min per success and over a million tokens per episode, whereas RoboThink needs 55 s and 8k tokens. The same recipe works across policies, for both vision-language-action models and world action models, and across robots, from one arm to two arms and a mobile manipulator. On all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with two arms, success rises from 0.12 to 0.74 under the constant drift and from 0.31 to 0.56 under the random one. Finally, the agent is a plug-in. A policy taught by one agent works with other agents, including open-weight ones, and grows stronger with a stronger agent, without retraining.

summary.en: RoboThink lets an agent think while a policy acts: the agent rewrites instructions and supplies motion feedback trained via agent-labelled DAgger, raising LIBERO success from 0.09 to 0.87 under drift with 55 s and 8k tokens per success.
summary.zh: RoboThink 让智能体负责思考、策略网络负责执行：智能体通过指令通道改写任务指令、通过反馈通道给动作反馈，借助 agent-labelled DAgger 训练；在 LIBERO 上把恒定漂移下的成功率从 0.09 提到 0.87，在 RoboTwin 2.0 双臂任务上从 0.12 提到 0.74，单个成功仅需 55 秒和 8k tokens。

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
papers.abstract: Broadly speaking, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training converts compute into model capabilities by training on model-generated data. Typically, the rollouts are discarded after each update, and the knowledge acquired during RL resides in the model weights. In this work, we investigate how much of this knowledge is retained in the rollouts themselves. A natural first attempt is to replay the original RL algorithm on archived (rather than freshly generated) rollouts, but this generally leads to catastrophic collapse. We provide a simple explanation for this phenomenon, which in turn suggests a remedy we call maximum likelihood replay: fitting the model to its archived rollouts. Surprisingly, starting from the same base model and replaying the rollouts in the order in which they were generated, without any distinction between correct and incorrect responses, is sufficient to recover the performance of online RL. In fact, a single maximum likelihood update per rollout batch closely tracks the entire learning curve of online RL. Furthermore, maximum likelihood replay on the rollouts of the last few RL steps often suffices to recover the final model's performance. This suggests that much of the compute invested in RL goes into discovering an improved sampling distribution rather than learning it from samples.

summary.en: Investigating how much RL-acquired knowledge persists in rollouts, maximum likelihood replay that fits archived rollouts in generation order without distinguishing correct responses matches online RL performance.
summary.zh: 研究RL后训练产生的rollout中保留多少知识，发现直接用最大似然拟合归档rollout（maximum likelihood replay），不区分对错、按生成顺序回放，即可复现在线RL的性能，单次更新即可追踪完整学习曲线。

papers.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
papers.abstract: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. We trace these failures to the asymmetry between reading and modification directions during erasure, which yields non-normal erase operators whose directional gains accumulate across tokens, triggering exponential state growth even without new writes. To resolve this, we propose \model{}, employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility. Theoretically, we establish an $O(\sqrt{T})$ upper bound on recurrent state growth while retaining chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that \model{} achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting and average accuracy across nine downstream tasks by 0.62 points in the hybrid setting.

summary.en: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2 fixes GDN-2's exponential recurrent state growth via symmetric erasure and decay-regulated residual writing, with an O(√T) bound. On 1.6B models it raises 128K RULER by 6.80 and nine-task accuracy by 0.62.
summary.zh: 针对 Gated DeltaNet-2 长上下文训练中擦除方向不对称导致循环状态指数增长的问题，提出 Stable Gated DeltaNet-2，用对称擦除保证非扩张状态传播，并配合衰减调节的残差写入，理论上给出 O(√T) 状态增长上界且保留分块并行。1.6B 参数模型上训练稳定，128K 平均 RULER 分数提升 6.80 分，九个下游任务平均准确率提升 0.62 分。

papers.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
papers.abstract: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3\% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points. It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Beyond performance, controlled interventions indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation. These results provide both a practical recipe for building strong frontier-model-as-policy harnesses and a clearer account of the capabilities that drive their performance.

summary.en: Embo-Harness systematically studies frontier multimodal models as closed-loop robot policies, distilling six findings; it reaches 83.3% success on RoboLab-120, beating the best baseline by 26.2 points, and solves 15 of 20 zero-shot real-world trials.
summary.zh: Embo-Harness 系统研究前沿多模态模型直接作为机器人策略的闭环框架，梳理提示、规划、动作执行与工具使用四个环节并总结六条经验，在 RoboLab-120 上取得 83.3% 成功率，超最强基线 26.2 个百分点，真实世界四项操作任务零样本 20 次试验成功 15 次。

papers.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
papers.abstract: Agentic Robotics, in which foundation models act as coding agents to control robots through executable programs, has emerged as a compelling paradigm for embodied intelligence. Yet unlike software engineering, where massive executable environments power post-training, robotics remains constrained by small, manual benchmarks and in-distribution evaluation. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboUniverse-10K, 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments built from real-world videos via an automated Real2Sim and quality assurance pipeline. Each runs in an isolated, Harbor-compatible harness that hides privileged states and grading logic to mirror real-world sensing. From the same pipeline, we hold out 500 unseen tasks to establish RoboUniverse-Verified, an expert-verified zero-shot benchmark. Evaluating 11 closed- and open-source models reveals a huge gap: frontier models reach 85.8\% success, while open-source baselines lag at 2.6\% to 10.0\%, bottlenecked by low-level grasping, deformable-object manipulation, and post-contact physical control. Finally, we collect about 17K multi-turn trajectories totaling 0.79B tokens with GPT-6 Astra and perform full-parameter supervised fine-tuning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, yielding RoboUniverse-35B-A3B. Our model achieves substantial zero-shot gains on RoboUniverse-Verified, lifting the success rate from 0.8\% to 21.2\%, while achieving zero-shot task completions across LIBERO-MAX, RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0, and a real Franka arm. We open-source the RL-ready environments and model to lay the foundation for large-scale reinforcement learning in Agentic Robotics.

summary.en: RoboUniverse-10K builds 10,807 resettable, verifiable physics environments from real videos via automated Real2Sim, plus a 500-task zero-shot benchmark where frontier models hit 85.8% versus 2.6-10.0% for open baselines; fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B lifts success from 0.8% to 21.2%.
summary.zh: RoboUniverse-10K 通过自动化 Real2Sim 与质检流程从真实视频构建 10,807 个可交互、可重置、可验证的物理环境，并留出 500 个任务组成 RoboUniverse-Verified 零样本基准；11 个模型评测中前沿模型成功率 85.8%，开源基线仅 2.6%–10.0%；再用约 17K 多轮轨迹微调 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 得到 RoboUniverse-35B-A3B，零样本成功率从 0.8% 提升到 21.2%。

papers.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
papers.abstract: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

summary.en: Posterior Matching Distillation combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation by matching exponentially tilted student sample means, achieving the best 4-step FID on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B.
summary.zh: PMD 将模式覆盖的后验采样与任意步数生成结合，通过匹配指数重加权学生样本均值来学习教师后验，在 SDXL 和 FLUX.2 [klein] 4B 上取得 4 步方法中最佳 FID。

papers.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
papers.abstract: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. In this work, we investigate how to effectively mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope. We reveal a mixing trade-off: when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixed residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other. We theoretically validate our findings by bounding the cumulative residual mixing, stream difference and gradient difference of mixing coefficients across layers. Motivated by these findings, we propose Contraction for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (cmHC), an exact doubly stochastic method which geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior. This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization. Moreover, we apply a moderate contraction at the shallow layers to prevent over-mixing, enabling stable gradient propagation on extremely large-scale model pretraining. Extensive experiments across dense and mixture-of-experts models at various parameter scales demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of cmHC. We also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs, reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.

summary.en: CmHC geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope inward to mix residual streams, mitigating under- and over-mixing; it stabilizes pretraining of dense and MoE models and cuts hyper-connection latency by up to 44.8% on Ascend NPUs.
summary.zh: cmHC 通过将 Birkhoff 多面体几何收缩到内部来混合残差流，缓解 under-mixing 与 over-mixing 的权衡，在稠密和 MoE 模型预训练中稳定梯度传播，并在 Ascend NPU 上将超连接执行延迟降低最多 44.8%。

papers.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
papers.abstract: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer

summary.en: Loom attention interweaves vertical attention over prior head outputs via normalized gated linear attention with horizontal token attention, yielding LoomFormer; with only ~2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B reaches ~1.6x mHC-Pythia-2.8B's downstream gain and matches Pythia-12B zero-shot.
summary.zh: Loom attention 通过垂直注意力对前序 head 输出做归一化门控线性注意力，并与水平 token 注意力交织，实现逐 token 动态重连电路，构成 LoomFormer 双流架构；在 300B token、仅增约 2% FLOPs 下，LoomPythia-2.8B 下游增益约为 mHC-Pythia-2.8B 的 1.6 倍，0-shot 追平 Pythia-12B。

papers.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
papers.abstract: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical pretraining, staged supervised fine-tuning, and adaptive reinforcement learning. Across this curriculum, progressive supervised refinement and adaptive reinforcement learning yield consistent stage-wise gains, substantially advancing both specialized visual understanding and medical language capabilities. Evaluated against 77 competing models across 238 clinical tasks spanning 61 public and 13 private multi-center benchmarks in more than 40 modalities, Sage-Med-Preview achieves an average score of 58.26% on the 31 public multimodal benchmarks. It outperforms the state-of-the-art open-source medical model Hulu-Med-235B-A22B at 50.99% and the general scientific model Intern-S2-Preview at 52.24%, and approaches the advanced proprietary model GPT-6.2-Sol across multiple tasks such as comprehensive multimodal understanding, report generation, and visual grounding. Although substantial challenges remain in complex medical reasoning and multi-step clinical workflows, this report provides empirical evidence, actionable data and training recipes, and a rigorous benchmark toward scalable clinical multimodal intelligence.

summary.en: Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter (3B activated) medical MLLM trained via curated 322.7M-record data and a progressive pretraining-to-SFT-to-RL curriculum, scores 58.26% on 31 public multimodal benchmarks, beating Hulu-Med-235B-A22B (50.99%) and Intern-S2-Preview (52.24%).
summary.zh: Sage-Med-Preview 是 35B 参数（激活 3B）的医学多模态模型，用 3.227 亿条候选数据分阶段筛选结合医学预训练、分阶段监督微调与自适应强化学习的渐进课程训练，在 31 个公开多模态基准上均分 58.26%，超过 Hulu-Med-235B-A22B 的 50.99% 和 Intern-S2-Preview 的 52.24%。

papers.title: Attention Latent Feedback
papers.abstract: During autoregressive decoding, the deeper representations of the previous token have already been computed, yet shallow layers at the current token cannot read them directly because standard self-attention connects positions only at the same depth. We introduce Attention Latent Feedback (ALF), an architecture that allows every sublayer to attend to the outputs of the deeper layers at the previous position. Training unrolls this cross-position recurrence into two parallel passes, whereas decoding remains single-pass using cached previous-token states. Across mixture-of-experts models with up to 4.0B parameters, ALF lowers held-out loss by 0.022-0.024 nats over the standard residual with about 1.1% decoding FLOP overhead, and consistently outperforms prior final-state feedback across all three scales on both standard and attention residual backbones. On MoE-1.6B, ALF matches a $1.38\times$ larger baseline token budget, and on MoE-4.0B it lifts average accuracy across seventeen downstream benchmarks from 45.1% to 47.0%. Analysis further reveals that intermediate and nearby deeper layers drive most of this benefit, allowing a fixed nearest-window variant to retain 89%-94% of the gain at linear read cost while learned attention widens its margin with scale.

summary.en: Attention Latent Feedback lets each sublayer attend to deeper layers' outputs at the previous position, lowering held-out loss by 0.022-0.024 nats at ~1.1% decoding FLOP overhead and lifting MoE-4.0B average accuracy from 45.1% to 47.0%.
summary.zh: Attention Latent Feedback (ALF) 让每个子层关注前一个位置更深层的输出，训练时展开为两遍并行计算、解码仍为单遍；在最多 4.0B 参数的 MoE 模型上使 held-out loss 比标准残差降低 0.022–0.024 nats，解码 FLOP 开销约 1.1%，MoE-4.0B 在十七个下游基准上平均准确率从 45.1% 提升到 47.0%。

papers.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
papers.abstract: Computer-using agents are increasingly expected to complete realistic user goals rather than isolated GUI actions. However, existing benchmarks typically isolate web, mobile, or desktop environments, leaving it unclear whether a single generalist agent can execute long-horizon workflows that span multiple operating systems and persistent application states. We introduce OS-Omni, a live cross-platform benchmark and execution environment for evaluating computer-using agents across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web environments. OS-Omni is released in versioned waves of 300 tasks each; this paper focuses on the first release, v1, which contains 48 tasks per platform and 12 cross-platform workflows that pair a desktop with an Android phone. OS-Omni provides reproducible initialization, platform-specific adapters, trajectory logging, and executable final-state evaluators, and includes controlled service-backed applications for workflows involving account, cart, budget, calendar, message, and other persistent state. Human studies show that OS-Omni tasks require 67.54 interaction steps, substantially exceeding OSWorld references of 15.0 steps. On v1, the strongest evaluated agent, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches 68.5% average success, trailing the 77.3% human reference by 8.8 points; the gap is uneven across platforms, with frontier models exceeding humans on Linux but trailing them by more than 25 points on iOS and macOS. These results indicate that current agents remain far from platform-robust, long-horizon computer use, especially when success requires sustained state tracking and durable final-state changes.

summary.en: OS-Omni is a live cross-platform benchmark for computer-using agents spanning Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web; its v1 has 48 tasks per platform plus 12 cross-platform workflows averaging 67.54 steps. Claude Opus 5.5 scores 68.5% versus 77.3% human, trailing by over 25 points on iOS and macOS.
summary.zh: OS-Omni 是覆盖 Windows、Ubuntu、macOS、iOS、Android 和 Web 的跨平台计算机代理实时基准，v1 每平台 48 个任务、另含 12 个跨平台工作流，任务平均需 67.54 步；最强代理 Claude Opus 5.5 平均成功率 68.5%，低于人类 77.3%，在 iOS 和 macOS 上差距超过 25 点。

papers.title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. However, this power has so far required training from scratch and yielded only modest gains for LLMs. Finetuning existing models into loops is far cheaper, yet also brings only marginal gains over SFT. We propose LoopRes, an effective, scalable, and simple approach that turns loops into significant and consistent gains for pretrained LLMs. Building on Attention Residuals, LoopRes lets each looped layer attend directly to the outputs of earlier loops. Since these outputs are iterates of the same layers and become harder to tell apart, we give each a trainable loop-aware key that encodes its structural identity. Attending to all earlier loops also lets layers skip intermediate ones, so we restrict each layer to a residual window of the latest W loops, forcing every loop to build incrementally on recent ones. Across 6 pretrained LLMs from 3 model families and 9 benchmarks, LoopRes delivers significant and consistent gains: at 2x compute, it improves Qwen3-1.7B-Base by 29.1% over SFT, more than doubling the gain of the state-of-the-art baseline. The gains hold on larger models up to 30B and across all three families. More importantly, from 1.7B to 8B, LoopRes scales more steeply than SFT as compute grows, reaching a higher ceiling while needing less compute on long outputs. These results establish LoopRes as an effective looping approach, delivering both better performance and better test-time scaling.

summary.en: LoopRes lets looped layers attend to earlier loops with trainable loop-aware keys and a residual window W; on 6 pretrained LLMs and 9 benchmarks it beats SFT by 29.1% on Qwen3-1.7B-Base at 2x compute and scales better.
summary.zh: LoopRes 通过让循环层关注此前各循环输出并引入可训练循环感知 key、限制残差窗口 W，将循环式微调用于预训练 LLM；在 6 个模型、9 个基准上，2 倍计算下 Qwen3-1.7B-Base 较 SFT 提升 29.1%，超过最强基线增益两倍，且在 30B 以内及三个模型家族上稳定，测试时扩展更优。

papers.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a powerful approach for improving language-model reasoning, but its supervision is inherently sparse: a sequence-level verifier reward is propagated only through sampled trajectories and provides no direct signal for alternative actions. On-policy distillation (OPD) offers a complementary form of supervision by providing dense teacher feedback over the full next-token distribution, but this signal is not grounded in verified task outcomes. Simply co-optimizing the two objectives does not couple these signals: verifier feedback remains sparse and does not inform the dense teacher supervision. We introduce Verifiable On-Policy Distillation (VOPD), which transfers sparse verifier feedback into dense, verifier-grounded supervision. Our key observation is that the implicit-reward view of OPD places teacher supervision and verifier feedback in a common reward space while retaining a reward signal available for every next-token action. Under this view, VOPD projects verifier preference onto the teacher's implicit-reward direction and Rao--Blackwellizes the resulting signal over the full vocabulary, propagating verifier-grounded supervision to actions that were never sampled. The resulting objective can also be interpreted as adaptively extrapolating the distillation target according to teacher--verifier agreement. Across two teacher--student configurations and eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VOPD consistently improves both final performance and learning efficiency over vanilla OPD and other on-policy distillation baselines. Our code is available at https://github.com/juntongshi48/VOPD.

summary.en: VOPD projects sparse verifier preferences onto the teacher's implicit-reward direction and Rao-Blackwellizes them over the vocabulary for dense verifier-grounded supervision, improving final performance and learning efficiency over vanilla OPD and other on-policy distillation baselines on eight math reasoning benchmarks.
summary.zh: VOPD 将稀疏的验证器奖励投影到教师的隐式奖励方向上，并在整个词表上做 Rao-Blackwell 化，得到稠密的、基于验证器的监督信号，在八项数学推理基准上相比 vanilla OPD 与其他 on-policy distillation 基线同时提升最终性能与学习效率。

papers.title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly work as teams of agents, and a team is expected to solve problems beyond the reach of any single member. Most evaluations credit a team for outperforming a single agent, without accounting for the additional computation: a team may consume many times the tokens of one agent, and a plain vote over independent answers already explains most of the reported gain. Two questions therefore remain open: When does interaction itself make a group smarter, and can a group improve its next generation by learning from its own work? We answer both with the equal-budget ladder, which grades a group against independent agents at three levels: outperforming a single agent, a compute-matched majority vote, and compute-matched pass@n. On this ladder we define Recursive Collective Intelligence (RCI) as a group whose own output, without a teacher or external labels, makes its next generation smarter at equal cost. Three findings follow. First, interaction improves collective intelligence when it moves information across agents: forwarding split facts lifts groups above pass@n at three model scales, by about a third at 27B. Second, organization emerges spontaneously: identical 27B agents form hubs and improve accuracy by 18 percentage points; encoding their organization in a prompt enables them to reach level 3 at less than half the token budget in a descriptive comparison. Third, groups recursively improve themselves: Two label-free generations progressively climb the ladder, the second 9B generation surpassing both pass@$n$ and a control trained on base-model turns; on PlanBench, HiddenBench and Hanabi, each generation outperforms its predecessor on unseen problems for four to six generations. A group therefore outperforms its members when it forwards useful information more efficiently than it spends tokens on coordination, and learns to do so from its own work.

summary.en: The equal-budget ladder grades multi-agent LLM teams against a single agent, compute-matched majority vote, and pass@n; recursively self-trained groups, which forward split facts, beat pass@n by ~1/3 at 27B, gain 18 points from emergent hubs, and improve for 4-6 generations.
summary.zh: 等算力阶梯（equal-budget ladder），在单智能体、算力对齐多数投票与算力对齐 pass@n 三级上衡量多智能体团队，并定义 Recursive Collective Intelligence（RCI）：无教师、无外部标签，团队用自身输出让下一代同等成本更聪明；转发拆分事实可在 27B 上超 pass@n 约三分之一，同质 27B 智能体自发形成枢纽使准确率提升 18 个百分点，两代无标签训练在 PlanBench、HiddenBench、Hanabi 上连续 4–6 代优于前代。

papers.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
papers.abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are post-trained and deployed as agents inside a "harness", but standard harness designs accumulate context that the neural network is forced to generalize to, making training for long-horizon tasks expensive and time-consuming. We study an alternative emerging path: training inherently neurosymbolic LM harnesses, which externalize and manage context programmatically to compose existing LM capabilities. We hypothesize that training around these harnesses can offer a better return on compute by enabling compositional generalization, as they can learn to decompose complex problems so that every observation their neural LM receives is locally in-distribution, even when the full task is novel. We find that harnesses like the Recursive Language Model (RLM) learn such decompositions readily under reinforcement learning post-training: (1) we demonstrate that training only on short tasks can generalize to tasks 2-64$\times$ longer while the base neural LM improves less, and (2) training on one domain transfers to novel domains that share latent structure. On messier, complex tasks, we find that we can target individual LLM calls within a harness by generating and training on easier, synthetically generated surrogate environments with fake tool / sub-calls, a technique we call surrogate harness training. From this finding, we train RLM-27B on synthetic data, and show it improves Qwen3.8-27B in the same RLM harness on a hard suite of long-context tasks like CTC-Bench and ExpertLongBench by 26.9% on average while using $\sim$2$\times$ fewer tokens at inference time. Finally, we show that harnesses can compose over these newly learned decompositions using recursive sub-harness calls.

summary.en: Training neurosymbolic LM harnesses like RLM with RL on short tasks generalizes to 2-64x longer ones; RLM-27B, trained on synthetic data, beats Qwen3.8-27B by 26.9% on CTC-Bench and ExpertLongBench with ~2x fewer inference tokens.
summary.zh: 研究以神经符号式 harness 管理上下文的组合泛化能力：仅用短任务强化学习训练 RLM，即可泛化到长 2-64 倍的任务；用合成数据训练 RLM-27B，在 CTC-Bench 和 ExpertLongBench 上平均提升 Qwen3.8-27B 26.9%，推理 token 约减半。

papers.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
papers.abstract: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid ($>250\times$ dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension ($d \to d+K$) with $\sqrt{d/(d+K)}$ norm compensation, Base-1000 canonical BPE emission, and differential $(+254,-256)$ tied unembeddings. An automated 5-stage compiler synthesizes 4-8 digit signed $\{+,-,\times\}$ circuits in constant $\mathsf{TC}^0$ depth alongside 3-literal Boolean (100%, $N=1{,}728$; plus 42-layer Gemma 4 E4B audits) and 5-bit Majority/Parity (100%) circuits. On 6-digit arithmetic ($N=1{,}200$, BF16), IBM Granite 4.2 3B (1.07M-1.33M active non-zeros, $\le 0.036\%$) and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B (2.25M-2.39M non-zeros, $\le 0.057\%$) reach 99.17% and 100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy (100% with an FP32 sidecar) and 98%-100% mid-sentence resumption, outperforming 12.8K-sample LoRA (42.2% / 61.7%, 0% inline continuation). A factorized block-sparse sidecar holds A100 memory at 7.89 / 10.65 GiB (4.60 / 8.14 GiB under INT8/INT4 + FP32 sidecar) while passing all 14/14 pre-registered $>2$K-token Tango splits ($N=4{,}392$; 0/11,134 OOD triggers).

summary.en: Closed-form zero-gradient circuit-grafting compiles exact multi-digit arithmetic and Boolean/majority circuits into pretrained LM weights without training data or runtime hooks; Granite 4.2 3B and Qwen 3.5 4B reach 99.17%/100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy versus 42.2%/61.7% for 12.8K-sample LoRA.
summary.zh: 闭式零梯度电路嫁接原语将精确多位数算术与布尔/多数/奇偶电路直接编译进预训练权重，无需训练样本或运行时钩子；IBM Granite 4.2 3B 与 Qwen 3.5 4B 在 6 位数算术上达 99.17%/100.00% ALU 前缀准确率，远超 12.8K 样本 LoRA 的 42.2%/61.7%。

papers.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT

summary.en: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer reuses keys and values as memory across depths and loops; U-MoLT beats OLMo3 with 1.7x CE token efficiency at 700M and +2.1 points on 10-task accuracy at 3B MoE.
summary.zh: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer 用 Mixture-of-Loops Attention 把 KV 当作跨深度和循环复用记忆，其 U-MoLT 变体在 400B token 预训练中于 700M 模型上比 OLMo3 达到 1.7 倍的验证交叉熵 token 效率，3B MoE 困惑度降低 0.75、10 项任务准确率提升 2.1 个百分点。

papers.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
papers.abstract: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention. To enable efficient inference, we further develop an execution scheme tailored to this architecture, combining CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and execution-flow simplification while preserving the canonical history update. Evaluations on retargeted HiPHI demonstrate accurate terminal control over rollouts of up to 39.52 s, while short-horizon comparisons on BONES Seed and retargeted HumanML3D show that the model also retains strong spatial control and text-motion matching. On an RTX 4090, the optimized execution reduces median complete-window latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms, achieving a median paired speedup of 6.138$\times$ while preserving identical outputs and committed states in the tested rollouts. Moreover, we conduct extensive real-world evaluation on the Unitree G1, demonstrating sequential text-guided action composition, expressive motion, and interactive locomotion through keyboard and mouse control.

summary.en: Motion Mamba 2.0 combines Mamba recurrent states with persistent content memory for autoregressive root-body diffusion, enabling terminal control over 39.52 s rollouts; CUDA Graph optimizations cut latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms (6.138x median speedup), validated on Unitree G1.
summary.zh: Motion Mamba 2.0 用 Mamba 循环状态加持久内容记忆 PCM 做根-身体扩散式自回归动作生成，支持最长 39.52 s 的长程末端控制；配合 CUDA Graph 等优化，RTX 4090 上完整窗口延迟从 1685.35 ms 降到 276.14 ms，中位加速 6.138 倍，并在 Unitree G1 上验证了文本引导动作组合与交互式行走。

papers.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
papers.abstract: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/

summary.en: Depth Pro 2 trains one scalable network on images and video to predict native-resolution depth that is metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent, outperforming prior work and redefining the Pareto frontier.
summary.zh: Depth Pro 2 用单一可扩展网络统一处理图像与视频，以原生分辨率预测稠密深度，同时兼顾度量精度、边界锐利度与时序一致性，在四项指标上超越先前方法并重划 Pareto 前沿。

papers.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.

summary.en: Mind2Act World is a 30-task, 180-configuration diagnostic manipulation benchmark with Mind, Act, and Mind2Act views; the best agent scores 52.7% and 39.0% but only 12.0% on Mind2Act.
summary.zh: Mind2Act World 构建 30 个仿真操作任务、180 种配置的诊断基准，分 Mind、Act、Mind2Act 三视角评测多模态智能体、VLA 与 WAM；最强智能体在 Mind 与 Act 上分别成功 52.7% 和 39.0%，Mind2Act 仅 12.0%。

papers.title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act
papers.abstract: Robot policies act in real time but fail without knowing why, whereas a reasoning agent that watches the robot can often tell what went wrong. Existing systems either hand the agent control, which takes minutes per episode, or let it send instructions. Yet a policy follows a new instruction only from a fresh start, since a half-finished task leaves it in states outside its training data. Nor can an instruction fix how the robot moves. If a drift keeps pulling the hand to the left, "push right, slightly" is not a task the policy has learned. We propose RoboThink, in which the agent thinks and the policy learns to act on the agent's guidance. An instruction channel tells the policy what to do. When the user says "the milk, not the butter" after the robot has started, the agent rewrites the instruction and the robot undoes its own motion, with no training. A feedback channel tells it how to move. It is taught from the agent alone with agent-labelled DAgger, role tokens and counterfactual feedback, and is read only by the policy's action module. On LIBERO, RoboThink with Claude Opus 5.5 raises success from 0.09 to 0.87 under an unknown constant drift and from 0.42 to 0.84 under a random one. It also completes misheard and changed requests in 0.91 to 1.00 of the episodes. Acting alone, GPT-6 Astra needs 2.1 min per success and over a million tokens per episode, whereas RoboThink needs 55 s and 8k tokens. The same recipe works across policies, for both vision-language-action models and world action models, and across robots, from one arm to two arms and a mobile manipulator. On all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with two arms, success rises from 0.12 to 0.74 under the constant drift and from 0.31 to 0.56 under the random one. Finally, the agent is a plug-in. A policy taught by one agent works with other agents, including open-weight ones, and grows stronger with a stronger agent, without retraining.

summary.en: RoboThink lets an agent think while a policy acts: the agent rewrites instructions and supplies motion feedback trained via agent-labelled DAgger, raising LIBERO success from 0.09 to 0.87 under drift with 55 s and 8k tokens per success.
summary.zh: RoboThink 让智能体负责思考、策略网络负责执行：智能体通过指令通道改写任务指令、通过反馈通道给动作反馈，借助 agent-labelled DAgger 训练；在 LIBERO 上把恒定漂移下的成功率从 0.09 提到 0.87，在 RoboTwin 2.0 双臂任务上从 0.12 提到 0.74，单个成功仅需 55 秒和 8k tokens。

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
papers.abstract: Broadly speaking, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training converts compute into model capabilities by training on model-generated data. Typically, the rollouts are discarded after each update, and the knowledge acquired during RL resides in the model weights. In this work, we investigate how much of this knowledge is retained in the rollouts themselves. A natural first attempt is to replay the original RL algorithm on archived (rather than freshly generated) rollouts, but this generally leads to catastrophic collapse. We provide a simple explanation for this phenomenon, which in turn suggests a remedy we call maximum likelihood replay: fitting the model to its archived rollouts. Surprisingly, starting from the same base model and replaying the rollouts in the order in which they were generated, without any distinction between correct and incorrect responses, is sufficient to recover the performance of online RL. In fact, a single maximum likelihood update per rollout batch closely tracks the entire learning curve of online RL. Furthermore, maximum likelihood replay on the rollouts of the last few RL steps often suffices to recover the final model's performance. This suggests that much of the compute invested in RL goes into discovering an improved sampling distribution rather than learning it from samples.

summary.en: Investigating how much RL-acquired knowledge persists in rollouts, maximum likelihood replay that fits archived rollouts in generation order without distinguishing correct responses matches online RL performance.
summary.zh: 研究RL后训练产生的rollout中保留多少知识，发现直接用最大似然拟合归档rollout（maximum likelihood replay），不区分对错、按生成顺序回放，即可复现在线RL的性能，单次更新即可追踪完整学习曲线。

papers.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
papers.abstract: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. We trace these failures to the asymmetry between reading and modification directions during erasure, which yields non-normal erase operators whose directional gains accumulate across tokens, triggering exponential state growth even without new writes. To resolve this, we propose \model{}, employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility. Theoretically, we establish an $O(\sqrt{T})$ upper bound on recurrent state growth while retaining chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that \model{} achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting and average accuracy across nine downstream tasks by 0.62 points in the hybrid setting.

summary.en: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2 fixes GDN-2's exponential recurrent state growth via symmetric erasure and decay-regulated residual writing, with an O(√T) bound. On 1.6B models it raises 128K RULER by 6.80 and nine-task accuracy by 0.62.
summary.zh: 针对 Gated DeltaNet-2 长上下文训练中擦除方向不对称导致循环状态指数增长的问题，提出 Stable Gated DeltaNet-2，用对称擦除保证非扩张状态传播，并配合衰减调节的残差写入，理论上给出 O(√T) 状态增长上界且保留分块并行。1.6B 参数模型上训练稳定，128K 平均 RULER 分数提升 6.80 分，九个下游任务平均准确率提升 0.62 分。

papers.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
papers.abstract: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe. This recipe prioritizes interfaces that exploit the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and identifies effective choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. On RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3\% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points. It also succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Beyond performance, controlled interventions indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation. These results provide both a practical recipe for building strong frontier-model-as-policy harnesses and a clearer account of the capabilities that drive their performance.

summary.en: Embo-Harness systematically studies frontier multimodal models as closed-loop robot policies, distilling six findings; it reaches 83.3% success on RoboLab-120, beating the best baseline by 26.2 points, and solves 15 of 20 zero-shot real-world trials.
summary.zh: Embo-Harness 系统研究前沿多模态模型直接作为机器人策略的闭环框架，梳理提示、规划、动作执行与工具使用四个环节并总结六条经验，在 RoboLab-120 上取得 83.3% 成功率，超最强基线 26.2 个百分点，真实世界四项操作任务零样本 20 次试验成功 15 次。

papers.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
papers.abstract: Agentic Robotics, in which foundation models act as coding agents to control robots through executable programs, has emerged as a compelling paradigm for embodied intelligence. Yet unlike software engineering, where massive executable environments power post-training, robotics remains constrained by small, manual benchmarks and in-distribution evaluation. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboUniverse-10K, 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments built from real-world videos via an automated Real2Sim and quality assurance pipeline. Each runs in an isolated, Harbor-compatible harness that hides privileged states and grading logic to mirror real-world sensing. From the same pipeline, we hold out 500 unseen tasks to establish RoboUniverse-Verified, an expert-verified zero-shot benchmark. Evaluating 11 closed- and open-source models reveals a huge gap: frontier models reach 85.8\% success, while open-source baselines lag at 2.6\% to 10.0\%, bottlenecked by low-level grasping, deformable-object manipulation, and post-contact physical control. Finally, we collect about 17K multi-turn trajectories totaling 0.79B tokens with GPT-6 Astra and perform full-parameter supervised fine-tuning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, yielding RoboUniverse-35B-A3B. Our model achieves substantial zero-shot gains on RoboUniverse-Verified, lifting the success rate from 0.8\% to 21.2\%, while achieving zero-shot task completions across LIBERO-MAX, RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0, and a real Franka arm. We open-source the RL-ready environments and model to lay the foundation for large-scale reinforcement learning in Agentic Robotics.

summary.en: RoboUniverse-10K builds 10,807 resettable, verifiable physics environments from real videos via automated Real2Sim, plus a 500-task zero-shot benchmark where frontier models hit 85.8% versus 2.6-10.0% for open baselines; fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B lifts success from 0.8% to 21.2%.
summary.zh: RoboUniverse-10K 通过自动化 Real2Sim 与质检流程从真实视频构建 10,807 个可交互、可重置、可验证的物理环境，并留出 500 个任务组成 RoboUniverse-Verified 零样本基准；11 个模型评测中前沿模型成功率 85.8%，开源基线仅 2.6%–10.0%；再用约 17K 多轮轨迹微调 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 得到 RoboUniverse-35B-A3B，零样本成功率从 0.8% 提升到 21.2%。

papers.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
papers.abstract: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

summary.en: Posterior Matching Distillation combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation by matching exponentially tilted student sample means, achieving the best 4-step FID on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B.
summary.zh: PMD 将模式覆盖的后验采样与任意步数生成结合，通过匹配指数重加权学生样本均值来学习教师后验，在 SDXL 和 FLUX.2 [klein] 4B 上取得 4 步方法中最佳 FID。

papers.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
papers.abstract: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. In this work, we investigate how to effectively mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope. We reveal a mixing trade-off: when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixed residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other. We theoretically validate our findings by bounding the cumulative residual mixing, stream difference and gradient difference of mixing coefficients across layers. Motivated by these findings, we propose Contraction for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (cmHC), an exact doubly stochastic method which geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior. This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization. Moreover, we apply a moderate contraction at the shallow layers to prevent over-mixing, enabling stable gradient propagation on extremely large-scale model pretraining. Extensive experiments across dense and mixture-of-experts models at various parameter scales demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of cmHC. We also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs, reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.

summary.en: CmHC geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope inward to mix residual streams, mitigating under- and over-mixing; it stabilizes pretraining of dense and MoE models and cuts hyper-connection latency by up to 44.8% on Ascend NPUs.
summary.zh: cmHC 通过将 Birkhoff 多面体几何收缩到内部来混合残差流，缓解 under-mixing 与 over-mixing 的权衡，在稠密和 MoE 模型预训练中稳定梯度传播，并在 Ascend NPU 上将超连接执行延迟降低最多 44.8%。

papers.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
papers.abstract: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer

summary.en: Loom attention interweaves vertical attention over prior head outputs via normalized gated linear attention with horizontal token attention, yielding LoomFormer; with only ~2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B reaches ~1.6x mHC-Pythia-2.8B's downstream gain and matches Pythia-12B zero-shot.
summary.zh: Loom attention 通过垂直注意力对前序 head 输出做归一化门控线性注意力，并与水平 token 注意力交织，实现逐 token 动态重连电路，构成 LoomFormer 双流架构；在 300B token、仅增约 2% FLOPs 下，LoomPythia-2.8B 下游增益约为 mHC-Pythia-2.8B 的 1.6 倍，0-shot 追平 Pythia-12B。
